summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose 37.3% YoY to ₹4,116 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5%, while raw-material and energy inflation remain a pass-through challenge.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income grew 31.1% YoY to ₹2,975 crores, with EBITDA up 13.7% to ₹371 crores (12.5% margin) and PAT up 20.5% to ₹210 crores. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA rose 30.8% to ₹598 crores, helped by Europe's best-ever quarter (EBITDA €21.9 million, 20.5% margin). Management said full-year standalone RMC rose 1.5 percentage points to 66.82% of revenue, and that ₹73.7 crores of aluminium and steel inflation was not passed through, which would have lifted FY26 EBITDA margin to 13.3% from 12.6%. Management expects Q1 FY27 to stay volatile on energy and metal costs and sees better numbers from Q2.

financial_highlights.value: ₹14,720 crores (EBITDA ₹2,090 crores, 14.2% margin; PAT ₹952 crores, 6.5% margin)

segments.name: Europe (Endurance Overseas)
segments.commentary: Q4 turnover €106.9 million (+33.6% YoY; ~7.4% excluding Stöferle) and EBITDA €21.9 million (20.5% margin, +49.1%). FY26 turnover €391.7 million (+28.9%) and EBITDA €72.4 million (18.5% margin).

segments.name: Stöferle (acquired April 2025)
segments.commentary: Q4 turnover €21 million, EBITDA €4.9 million, net result €2.6 million. FY26 (since acquisition) turnover €82.1 million, EBITDA €17.9 million, net result €8 million.

segments.name: Maxwell (battery management and electronics)
segments.commentary: FY26 record turnover ₹162 crores vs ₹70 crores in FY25; supplied 350,000 BMS units. Q4 EBITDA hit by a ₹6 crore provision on Hero Electric inventory; management says gross margin is safe excluding it. FY26 new orders ₹56 crores, cumulative ₹247 crores per annum.

segments.name: Brakes and ABS
segments.commentary: About 280,000 single-channel ABS units sold in FY26; management guides growth of 100-150% in FY27. Capacity expansion of 12 lakh units per annum with SOP expected September 2026. Dual-channel ABS SOP June 2026 for Bajaj Auto (120,000 units per annum), with a second 120,000-unit program in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Suspension
segments.commentary: Inverted front fork output to rise from 60,000 to 75,000 units per month by June 2026 and to 100,000 by end FY27. Demand is also rising for mono shocks.

segments.name: Aluminium castings and forging
segments.commentary: AURIC Shendra new orders translate into peak business potential of ₹513 crores per annum (peak FY29; plant expected to cross ₹200 crores in FY27). Chakan demand from Tata Motors and Mahindra rising 35-40%. A fifth aluminium forging press is being added at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, with SOP in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Alloy wheels (AURIC Bidkin and Chakan)
segments.commentary: Crossed 100,000 wheel sales in January 2026. Total capacity now 48 lakh wheel sets per annum. Bidkin is targeted to reach about ₹600 crores per annum sales by end Q3 or early Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Battery packs (Talegaon, Pune)
segments.commentary: Order for 2W EV battery packs worth ~₹300 crores per annum, potentially ₹350-360 crores. SOP planned for the last week of May 2026. Management said it could reach ₹600 crores per annum next FY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India capex expected to be similar to FY26 (~₹800 crores in FY26, up from ₹600 crores); automation is a key focus.
Q1 FY27 expected to be volatile on energy, aluminium and oil costs; management expects much better numbers from Q2 FY27 if the conflict eases.
Standalone EBITDA margin would have been 13.3% in FY26 excluding the ₹73.7 crore non-value-add aluminium and steel inflation.
Management aims to raise 4W share of revenue from about 6% in FY26 to 10% 'soon'.
Maharashtra incentive raised to ₹858 crores from ₹600 crores, to be availed over about seven years via state GST refund.
Chennai disc brake plant: Royal Enfield SOP July 2026, other OEMs from Q3 FY27. Tata Motors 4W drum brake and driveshaft SOPs in Q2 FY27 / June 2026.
capex_capacity: ABS capacity expansion of 12 lakh units per annum (existing 6.4 lakh), SOP September 2026, to proceed irrespective of final regulations.
Chennai brake plant: 3 million disc brake assemblies and 4 million discs per annum; Royal Enfield SOP July 2026. Group target is 7.6 million disc brake assemblies and 8.6 million discs per annum.
3W brake assembly volume to double from 0.6 million to 1.2 million units per annum by end of 2026.
New SMT line at Sambhajinagar for ABS ECUs and BMS, installation expected June 2026. Chennai die-casting plant to add a 1,600-ton die casting machine.
AURIC Shendra: US EV OEM SOP June 2026, JLR July-August 2026. Solar actuators to start H2 FY27 from new Sanand building. Driveshaft business to cross ₹100 crores in FY27.
demand_pricing: Domestic 2W sales in Q4 rose 25.4% YoY per SIAM, with scooters up 37.1% and motorcycles up 19.8%.
FY26 India order wins were ₹1,596 crores (₹1,579 crores new business), with 4W and non-auto about ₹743 crores. Q4 wins were ₹316 crores.

Pass-through is the main issue: aluminium alloy and oil and gas costs rose sharply from March and April 2026. Customers are being asked for spot increases; some OEMs have confirmed while others are pending.
Europe operates on a quarterly price reset based on prior-quarter averages, so the impact is mainly a margin-percentage effect (denominator). Management says there is no material risk.
Management claims it grew faster than peers in FY26: Bajaj +16.1% vs Bajaj 11.6%, Honda +16.9% vs 7.9%, Royal Enfield +32.7% vs 23.9%, TVS +29.1% vs 21.2%.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-time price impact in Q4 revenue, standalone or Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 RMC rose ₹160 crores (66.82% of revenue vs 65.3%), including ₹73.7 crores of non-pass-through aluminium and steel costs and ₹31.3 crores of outsourcing costs. Prior-year Q4 had about ₹25 crores of one-time gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ABS revenue trajectory with dual-channel SOP?
qa_highlights.answer: About 280,000 single-channel ABS units in FY26. Growth of 100-150% expected in FY27. The 12 lakh unit line will not be fully used initially.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for the greenfield plants and US EV OEM and JLR exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Bidkin alloy wheels reach peak in Q3-early Q4 FY27 (~₹600 crores p.a.). AURIC Shendra SOP for US EV OEM in June 2026 and JLR in July-August 2026, with FY27 revenue target above ₹200 crores. Battery pack SOP late May 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company set up manufacturing in the US or Europe given high European energy costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said customers want China-plus-one sourcing from India, so growth will come from AURIC Shendra, which has 11 acres plus 24 acres available for expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin headwinds behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 will still be volatile given rising oil, gas and alloy prices. It hopes the war ends next month, expects normalisation after that, and sees better numbers from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What edge does Endurance have in battery packs and BMS, given OEM backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited in-house patented busbar design and fully automatic lines for packs. It said very few players exist in pack and BMS. Management also said the pack solution was developed in-house and is for one OEM only.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stöferle order book and European growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Stöferle brought about €7 million of new business from Magna and BMW. Stöferle's annual run rate at acquisition was about €70-80 million. Excluding Stöferle, Q4 Europe grew 7.4% and FY26 grew 2%.

risks_watch: Pass-through risk: aluminium alloy, steel, gas and oil cost increases since March-April 2026 are still being negotiated with OEMs; some confirmations pending, and proprietary products carry a quarter lag.
Q1 FY27 expected to be volatile on energy, oil and alloy costs; management hopes the Middle East conflict ends next month and sees better numbers from Q2 FY27.

Ramp-up execution across multiple new plants: ABS 12 lakh unit line (SOP September 2026, not fully utilised initially), Chennai brake plant, battery packs (SOP last week of May 2026), AURIC Shendra and Bidkin wheels.
Maxwell: ₹6 crore Hero Electric inventory provision in Q4 after failed resolution; battery pack and BMS offering is new for the company and it is supplying one OEM initially.
Europe: ex-Stöferle growth slowed to 7.4% in Q4 and 2% for FY26, and Q4 margin of 20.5% was driven by higher volumes; energy costs remain about 3x 2021 levels.
Management aims to lift 4W share of revenue from about 6% to 10% 'soon', with no firm timeline given.
key_quotes: So, our dependence on gas has gone down, but of course gas for our surface treatments and all is still required.
Many OEMs have already confirmed the rates, some have given the emails or PO amendments, some are still awaited. It's a challenge when you ask for such large increases from customers.
I'm not at all concerned about the growth, but I'm definitely concerned about these cost increases in raw material and gas and oil and to be able to pass those on to our customers
So we have no intention to put up any plant in US or Europe because this is not what the customers are looking at.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, order wins and volumes, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly flagged raw-material and energy cost pressure and said pass-through to customers is still a work in progress. Answers on the battery pack edge and the 4W share target were more general, with few hard numbers.
